trials.label: r1c1
trials.name: reference hedged net
trials.hypothesis: This is the reference net from world 2, unchanged apart from the general K = (n_actions-1)/(Y*X). It reads the mask in 4 layouts and sums 4 re-laid output maps, using the reference recipe. It is the baseline the other candidates are measured against. If it scores 0 while a wider hedge scores above 0, this world's action layout is outside the 4 layouts it covers. If everything scores 0, the deviation is not in the layout.

trials.label: r1c2
trials.name: 16-layout hedge
trials.hypothesis: This widens the layout hedge to all 8 grid symmetries times type-major and type-minor action order: 16 layouts, on both the mask inputs and the output maps. It targets an action indexing that differs from the description in a way the 4 reference layouts miss. If it scores 0 while the reference scores above 0, or both score 0, layout order is not the deviation. If it beats the reference, the extra layouts matter.

trials.label: r1c3
trials.name: 5x5 head conv
trials.hypothesis: This is the reference net with a 5x5 head conv instead of 3x3, at about r=1.36. Each anchor logit then sees a 5x5 neighbourhood, which hedges footprints larger than described and anchors that are not top-left (centre or bottom-right). If it matches or trails the reference, footprints and anchors are not the bottleneck. If it is clearly higher (by more than about 0.07), they are.

trials.label: r1c4
trials.name: DONE-index hedge
trials.hypothesis: This bets that DONE sits at index 0 rather than last. The mask's placement part is read both as mask[:-1] and as mask[1:], each in the 4 reference layouts. Logits are summed from two arrangements, [placements, DONE] and [DONE, placements], each with its own head and DONE output. If it scores 0 when the reference also scores 0, the DONE position is not the deviation. If it scores above 0 while the reference scores 0, it is.

trials.label: r1c5
trials.name: obs symmetry hedge
trials.hypothesis: This bets that the obs is transposed, flipped or rotated relative to the mask and action grid. The stem takes the obs under all 8 grid symmetries (only the 4 flips if the grid is not square), plus the 4 reference mask layouts. A 1x1 stem already learns any channel order, so this is the bet that matters for the obs. If it scores 0 while the reference also scores 0, obs orientation is not the deviation.

trials.label: r1c6
trials.name: maximal combined hedge
trials.hypothesis: This combines every hedge: 16 action layouts, DONE at either end, obs under 8 symmetries and a 5x5 head, at about r=1.8 (about 135k steps). It targets a world that deviates in more than one way, or in a way only the union covers. If it scores above 0 while the single-hedge candidates score 0, the deviation is combined. If all candidates including this one score 0, the deviation lies outside these hedges (dynamics, grid size or reward), and next round should hedge those.

trials.label: r2c1
trials.name: obs-sym + 5x5 head
trials.hypothesis: This combines the two winning changes: obs under 8 symmetries plus a 5x5 head conv (r about 1.6). If their gains add up (orientation hedge and wider anchor/footprint context), it should beat 0.28 by more than 0.07. If it scores at or below 0.28, the 5x5 gain was noise or the smaller sample budget cancels it.

trials.label: r2c2
trials.name: obs-sym, 1 PPO epoch
trials.hypothesis: This is the obs-symmetry net with ppo_epochs 1 instead of 2, so it gets about 75% more samples (about 370k steps). Training and dev success match, so the agent seems sample-limited rather than overfitting. More fresh designs should help. If it scores at or below 0.28, the second epoch's sample reuse matters more than extra samples.

trials.label: r2c3
trials.name: obs-sym + 5x5, 1 epoch
trials.hypothesis: This combines obs symmetries, the 5x5 head and 1 PPO epoch. The single epoch offsets the 5x5 head's cost, giving about 270k steps instead of about 150k at 2 epochs. It bets that wider head context and more samples both help. If it trails the obs-sym net with 1 epoch, the 5x5 head is not worth its compute.

trials.label: r2c4
trials.name: obs-sym, 3 residual blocks
trials.hypothesis: This is the obs-symmetry net with a third residual 3x3 block (r about 1.4). The receptive field grows from 7x7 to 9x9, which covers the 8x8 grid, so the trunk can reason about support under overhangs and the order of placements. If it scores at or below 0.28 despite fewer steps, depth is not the bottleneck at this budget.

trials.label: r2c5
trials.name: obs-sym, longer horizon
trials.hypothesis: This is the obs-symmetry net with gamma 0.95 and gae_lambda 0.9 instead of 0.9 and 0.85. The +1 exact-build bonus comes at DONE, up to 33 placements later, and gamma 0.9 discounts it almost to nothing. A longer horizon should credit careful early placements and the DONE decision. If it scores at or below 0.28, value noise outweighs the longer credit assignment.

trials.label: r2c6
trials.name: obs-sym, identity layout only
trials.hypothesis: This is the obs-symmetry net with the mask input and output maps cut to the identity layout alone. It tests whether, once the obs symmetries are hedged, the transposed and flipped action layouts still matter or just add interference (the 16-layout version collapsed to 0). If it scores 0, the actions use a non-identity layout and the 4-layout hedge is needed. If it beats 0.28, the extra layouts were noise.

trials.label: r3c1
trials.name: r2c6 without obs symmetries
trials.hypothesis: This is r2c6 with the obs given only in its own orientation, which cuts the stem cost (r about 1.0, so about 240k steps). It tests whether the obs is actually reoriented relative to the actions, or whether the 8 symmetries only cost compute. If it scores at or above 0.85, the obs hedge is unneeded. import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"lr": 2e-3, "n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 8, "ppo_epochs": 2, "ent_coef": 0.002, "gamma": 0.9, "gae_lambda": 0.85}

OBS_SYM = False
HEAD_K = 3
HEAD_W = 32
STEM = 64
WIDTH = 40
NRES = 2


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Y = int(spec.Y)
        self.X = int(spec.X)
        self.N = int(spec.n_actions)
        self.P = self.N - 1
        YX = self.Y * self.X
        self.grid = (self.P % YX == 0)
        self.K = self.P // YX if self.grid else 0
        syms = []
        if OBS_SYM:
            for tr in ((0, 1) if self.Y == self.X else (0,)):
                for fy in (0, 1):
                    for fx in (0, 1):
                        syms.append((tr, fy, fx))
        else:
            syms.append((0, 0, 0))
        self.osyms = syms
        cin = int(spec.in_channels) * len(syms) + 2
        if self.grid:
            cin += self.K
        else:
            self.mask_embed = nn.Linear(self.N, 8 * YX)
            cin += 8
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, WIDTH, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.res = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1) for _ in range(NRES)])
        self.hconv = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HEAD_W, HEAD_K, padding=HEAD_K // 2)
        self.hskip = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HEAD_W, 1)
        if self.grid:
            self.hout = nn.Conv2d(HEAD_W, self.K, 1)
        else:
            self.hred = nn.Conv2d(HEAD_W, 8, 1)
            self.hlin = nn.Linear(8 * YX, self.P)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B = obs.shape[0]
        Y, X = self.Y, self.X
        feats = []
        for tr, fy, fx in self.osyms:
            o = obs
            if tr:
                o = o.transpose(2, 3)
            if fy:
                o = o.flip(2)
            if fx:
                o = o.flip(3)
            feats.append(o)
        m = mask.float()
        if self.grid:
            feats.append(m[:, :self.P].reshape(B, self.K, Y, X))
        else:
            feats.append(self.mask_embed(m).view(B, 8, Y, X))
        yy = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, Y, device=obs.device).view(1, 1, Y, 1).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        xx = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, X, device=obs.device).view(1, 1, 1, X).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        feats.append(yy)
        feats.append(xx)
        f = self.stem(torch.cat(feats, dim=1))
        for conv in self.res:
            f = F.relu(f + conv(f))
        h = F.relu(self.hconv(f) + self.hskip(f))
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        d = self.done_head(g)
        if self.grid:
            place = self.hout(h).reshape(B, -1)
        else:
            place = self.hlin(F.relu(self.hred(h)).flatten(1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, d], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

    tr, fy, fx = s
    if tr:
        o = o.transpose(2, 3)
    if fy:
        o = o.flip(2)
    if fx:
        o = o.flip(3)
    return o


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Y = int(spec.Y)
        self.X = int(spec.X)
        self.N = int(spec.n_actions)
        self.P = self.N - 1
        YX = self.Y * self.X
        self.grid = (self.P % YX == 0)
        self.K = self.P // YX if self.grid else 0
        syms = []
        for tr in ((0, 1) if self.Y == self.X else (0,)):
            for fy in (0, 1):
                for fx in (0, 1):
                    syms.append((tr, fy, fx))
        self.osyms = syms
        if OBS_PROJ > 0:
            self.oproj = nn.Conv2d(int(spec.in_channels), OBS_PROJ, 1)
            cobs = OBS_PROJ
        else:
            cobs = int(spec.in_channels)
        cin = cobs * len(syms) + 2
        if self.grid:
            cin += self.K
        else:
            self.mask_embed = nn.Linear(self.N, 8 * YX)
            cin += 8
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, WIDTH, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.res = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1) for _ in range(NRES)])
        self.hconv = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HEAD_W, HEAD_K, padding=HEAD_K // 2)
        self.hskip = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HEAD_W, 1)
        if self.grid:
            self.hout = nn.Conv2d(HEAD_W, self.K, 1)
        else:
            self.hred = nn.Conv2d(HEAD_W, 8, 1)
            self.hlin = nn.Linear(8 * YX, self.P)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B = obs.shape[0]
        Y, X = self.Y, self.X
        if OBS_PROJ > 0:
            base = self.oproj(obs)
        else:
            base = obs
        feats = [sym(base, s) for s in self.osyms]
        m = mask.float()
        if self.grid:
            feats.append(m[:, :self.P].reshape(B, self.K, Y, X))
        else:
            feats.append(self.mask_embed(m).view(B, 8, Y, X))
        yy = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, Y, device=obs.device).view(1, 1, Y, 1).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        xx = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, X, device=obs.device).view(1, 1, 1, X).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        feats.append(yy)
        feats.append(xx)
        f = self.stem(torch.cat(feats, dim=1))
        for conv in self.res:
            f = F.relu(f + conv(f))
        h = F.relu(self.hconv(f) + self.hskip(f))
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        d = self.done_head(g)
        if self.grid:
            place = self.hout(h).reshape(B, -1)
        else:
            place = self.hlin(F.relu(self.hred(h)).flatten(1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, d], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.2: The world deviates from its description, but the layout-hedged reference net learns here. The starting net scored 0, while the reference with 4 mask/output layouts scored 0.154 on dev. Two hedges did better. Adding the obs under all 8 grid symmetries scored 0.281, and the 5x5 head scored 0.246. Both differences from the reference are above the ~0.07 noise level, but each rests on one seed. Hedging DONE at both ends scored exactly the reference's 0.154, so the DONE position is not the deviation. The 16-layout hedge and the combined maximal hedge both scored 0. So summing many wrong-layout maps seems to hurt, and the action layout lies within the reference's 4 layouts. Training and dev success match, so there is no overfitting, and more samples may help. This round refines the obs-symmetry net, one change each: the 5x5 head, 1 PPO epoch, both together, a deeper trunk, a longer horizon, and pruning the layouts to identity only.
analyses.3: Ruled out: DONE sits at the last index, since r1c4's hedge for DONE at index 0 matched the reference. The action layout is the identity: cutting the mask and output layouts to identity alone (r2c6) jumped from 0.28 to 0.88. The 16-layout hedges gave 0, so the extra layouts were interference rather than coverage. It is still unclear whether the obs is oriented differently. Obs symmetries helped with 4 layouts (0.15 to 0.28), but that gap is close to noise. In round 2 the 5x5 head, a third residual block, 1 PPO epoch and gamma 0.95 were all tested on the weaker 4-layout net, and none helped there. This round refines r2c6 with one change per candidate: drop the obs symmetries (a cheaper net gets more steps), a 5x5 head, 3 residual blocks, width 48, 16 minibatches (more gradient steps at the same compute) and 3 PPO epochs. Training success (0.82) is still rising, which suggests the agent is short of samples or updates.
analyses.4:
What the results rule out and point to:
- The obs is reoriented relative to the actions. Without the obs symmetries r2c6 drops to 0 (r3c1).
- The mask and actions use the identity layout. Adding the 16-layout hedge gave 0, and the 4 extra layouts cut r2c6 from 0.88 to 0.28.
- The DONE index is not the deviation (r1c4 matched the reference).
- Refinements of r2c6 either matched it within noise (16 minibatches 0.83, width 48 0.84) or hurt: 3 epochs 0.69, 5x5 head 0.15, 3 residual blocks 0.32. Results look bimodal by seed, so the big drops may partly be bad seeds.
- 1 epoch hurt on the weaker net, so keep 2.
- Training success was still rising, so more steps or updates at r≈1 look most promising.

This round:
- Make the obs hedge cheaper: one learned 1x1 projection shared by all 8 symmetries cuts r and gives more steps.
- Test a few single-change recipe tweaks (lr, entropy, update count, rollout length) on the r2c6 net.
